record.paper_title: Confinement of color: open problems and perspectives.
record.context_brief: Order of the N_f=2 chiral transition
record.original_question: For QCD with two light quark flavors (N_f = 2), is the finite-temperature chiral transition first order or second order? In the scenario described in the paper, the answer depends on whether the axial U_A(1) symmetry is effectively restored below the chiral transition or only above it. This matters because a second-order chiral transition at zero quark mass would imply that the finite-mass line is a crossover, whereas a first-order chiral transition would allow the finite-mass deconfining transition to remain first order and hence compatible with an order-disorder picture of confinement.

evidence.quote: The region below the line is conventionally called confined, the region above it deconfined. A renormalization group analysis [5] shows that the chiral transition is first order for Nf ≥ 3 and can be second order or first order for Nf = 2 , depending on the fact that UA(1) symmetry is restored below or above the chiral transition.

Up to now lattice results were not conclusive on this point. New data [6] indicate that the transition is more compatible with first order . This is a fundamental question for our understanding of confinement and deserves further study.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider quantum chromodynamics (QCD) with two degenerate light quark flavors (N_f = 2) at finite temperature. In the limit of vanishing quark mass, the theory has an SU(2)_L × SU(2)_R chiral symmetry that is spontaneously broken at low temperature and restored at a finite critical temperature T_c. In addition, the classical U_A(1) axial symmetry is broken by the anomaly at zero temperature, but its effective restoration as a function of temperature is dynamical.

Determine the order of the finite-temperature chiral phase transition for N_f = 2 massless flavors. Specifically:

(a) Show, by a renormalization-group / Landau-Ginzburg-Wilson analysis of an effective theory for the chiral order parameter Φ (an N_f × N_f complex matrix transforming under SU(N_f)_L × SU(N_f)_R), that:
 - if the U_A(1) symmetry remains broken at T_c (so the effective theory has only SU(2)_L × SU(2)_R symmetry), then a second-order transition in the O(4) universality class is allowed;
 - if the U_A(1) symmetry is effectively restored at or below T_c (so the full U(2)_L × U(2)_R symmetry is realized on the order parameter), then no infrared-stable fixed point exists and the transition is driven first order.

(b) Decide which of these two scenarios is actually realized in N_f = 2 QCD, i.e. whether the chiral transition in the chiral limit is first order or second order, and correspondingly whether the physical finite-mass line is a crossover or admits a true first-order deconfinement/chiral transition.
artifact.status_search_result: The order of the N_f=2 chiral phase transition in the chiral limit remains an open problem. Recent lattice studies (through 2024–2025) give conflicting indications: some staggered-fermion analyses on N_τ ∈ {4,6,8} suggest the first-order regions shrink toward the continuum limit, favoring a second-order transition, while other works (including Wilson-fermion studies at imaginary chemical potential and effective-theory analyses tied to U_A(1) restoration) still leave both first- and second-order scenarios viable. The issue is explicitly described as long-standing and not resolved in the continuum limit.

status_evidence.title: The order of the chiral phase transition in massless many-flavour lattice QCD
status_evidence.snippet: The order of the thermal phase transition in the chiral limit of QCD with two dynamical flavors of quarks is a long-standing issue and still not known in the continuum limit.
status_evidence.claim: The N_f=2 chiral transition order is unresolved in the continuum limit.

status_evidence.title: Conjectures about the Chiral Phase Transition in QCD from Anomalous Multi-Instanton Interactions
status_evidence.snippet: The U(1)A anomaly controls the strength of the first order chiral transition for Nf = 2, 3, 4, and makes it almost indistinguishable from a second order one if it is sufficiently weak at the critical point.
status_evidence.claim: The role of U_A(1) restoration in determining the order remains under active theoretical investigation.

status_evidence.title: Progress on the QCD chiral phase transition for various numbers of flavors (Lattice 2024)
status_evidence.snippet: Lattice 2024 contribution on progress on the QCD chiral phase transition for various numbers of flavors and imaginary chemical potential.
status_evidence.claim: The question is still being actively studied on the lattice as of 2024.
